newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Bank Negara 1996 annual report.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank Negara 1996 annual report.

text.p: Following is a sampling of opinions about Malaysia's central Bank Negara's 1996 annual report published on Friday.
NIZAM IDRIS, ANALYST AT I.D.E.A. IN SINGAPORE
"The market will probably first focus on the current account deficit figure which was beyond (Finance Minister) Anwar Ibrahim's estimate.

"I suspect this would be bad for the ringgit. But the M3 money supply also looks quite bad. I suspect this could result in a rate hike later in the year, so this could be good for the ringgit. Overall, this could be negative on the stock market, as there are going to be fears of measures against property inflation and other types of inflation."
SANI HAMID, ANALYST AT MMS INTERNATIONAL IN SINGAPORE
"The BNM (Bank Negara Malaysia) annual report contains few surprises from the Ministry of Finance's October 1996 report and the set of economic figures released by Anwar in February.

"Only the current account deficit was much higher, at 13 billion ringgit, than Anwar's 11 billion ringgit. This is probably due to a new way to account for foreign workers' remittances, which we had anticipated."
PATRICK TAN, ASSISTANT DIRECTOR AT HG ASIA IN KUALA LUMPUR

"There doesn't seem to be many surprises. The current account deficit was up slightly, but this was probably due to certain lumpy import items, like ships and airplanes. Otherwise the report is quite neutral, with a bias towards tighter monetary policy.
"There could be more tightening of measures on the property market, but this should be viewed positively."
